Hexachlorophene may be used as a preservative in cosmetic products other than those which in normal use may be applied to mucous membranes

elements.quote: the term must be qualified by describing the cosmetic benefit provided by the sunscreen ingredient.
elements.note: 700.35 is a labeling-qualification rule for cosmetics that use the term sunscreen, not a prohibition or restriction of the ingredient.

completeness_note: Hexachlorophene is restricted in 21 CFR 250.250(e), which G does not cite and which is outside the Part 700 scope stated in the question. The cited range also holds restrictions J omits: zirconium aerosols (700.16(b)), CFC propellants (700.23, routed to 2.125) and prohibited cattle materials (700.27(b)(1)).
rationale: The supplemental text confirms the Part 700 restrictions for mercury, vinyl chloride, halogenated salicylanilides, chloroform and methylene chloride. Hexachlorophene is restricted only in 250.250(e), outside the Part 700 scope the question sets, and sunscreen is a labeling rule, so the row cannot be fixed by a citation change alone.
uncertainty: An SME could instead correct G to '21 CFR 700.11 through 700.35; 21 CFR 250.250(e)' and treat the Part 700 wording of the question as loose. That would leave the sunscreen element as the only open point.
needs_research_items: Decide whether to add 21 CFR 250.250(e) to G, given that the question is scoped to Part 700 and the hexachlorophene restriction sits in Part 250.
Decide whether 'sunscreens in cosmetics' belongs in a prohibited or restricted ingredient answer, since 700.35 only requires labeling qualification.
Decide whether J's omission of zirconium aerosols (700.16), CFC propellants (700.23) and prohibited cattle materials (700.27) makes the key unusable as a complete answer.
key_elements_issue: J lists hexachlorophene as a Part 700 restriction, but its restriction is in 21 CFR 250.250(e), not Part 700. J lists sunscreens as a restricted ingredient, but 700.35 only requires the term 'sunscreen' to be qualified in cosmetic labeling. J omits zirconium aerosols (700.16), CFC propellants (700.23) and prohibited cattle materials (700.27), all of which are in the cited range.
pass2_change: Decision unchanged (NEEDS_RESEARCH), but the open items are narrower. Supplemental 700.13, 700.14, 700.15, 700.18 and 700.19 moved five elements to SUPPORTED. Supplemental 250.250(e) confirmed that the hexachlorophene restriction exists outside Part 700. Supplemental 700.16, 700.23 and 700.27 confirmed restrictions that J omits.

rationale: The citation is right, but two J elements ('labeling limited to practitioner use' and 'advertising conditions') only loosely restate 801.109. The supplemental drug-rule text shows no separate advertising condition, which supports reading J's element as the 'advertised or represented' clause.
uncertainty: An SME may read 'advertising conditions' as the 'advertised or represented' clause in 801.109(c) and (d), and 'labeling limited to practitioner use' as 801.109(a). That reading would support ACCEPTED.
needs_research_items: Decide whether 'advertising conditions' is an acceptable paraphrase of the 801.109(c) and (d) requirement that practitioner information cover all advertised or represented purposes. Neither 801.109 nor the drug analog 201.100 states a separate advertising condition.
Decide whether 'labeling limited to practitioner use' faithfully states 801.109(a), which restricts possession and sale of the device, not its labeling.
key_elements_issue: 'Labeling limited to practitioner use' is not what 801.109(a) says: it restricts possession and sale of the device, not the labeling. 'Advertising conditions' has no separate basis in 801.109 beyond the requirement that information cover all advertised or represented purposes.
pass2_change: No change (NEEDS_RESEARCH). Supplemental 201.100 is the drug-labeling analog and does not govern devices. It shows the same 'advertised or represented' clause and no separate advertising condition, which narrows the remaining question to a paraphrase judgment.
